subject.title: Feature: Session authentication PIN gate (framework-level tool blocking)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core, opt-in session PIN gate that blocks tools until a trusted framework verifier authenticates the session?
rationale: This changes core config, secret handling, session state, and tool execution policy, so automation cannot choose the permanent security boundary or product semantics safely.

options.title: Sponsor a core opt-in PIN gate
options.body: Define the secret source, verifier command/tool, authenticated session state, reset behavior, and tests before allowing an implementation PR.

options.title: Keep it as a plugin/API discussion first
options.body: Require a plugin proof or missing-plugin-API proposal before adding any new core config or session state.

options.title: Reject PIN as a product direction
options.body: Document supported isolation, tool policy, sandboxing, and approval alternatives instead of adding a session PIN concept.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core opt-in PIN gate
recommendation.body: Define the secret source, verifier command/tool, authenticated session state, reset behavior, and tests before allowing an implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: He is listed for Agents, Hooks, and Security and recently touched the before_tool_call approval path that would enforce this boundary.
